global_caption: The video contains 9 shots and is a high-saturation pixel art-style tutorial on electronic soldering in a medieval magical castle tower workshop. The overall color scheme blends warm amber firelight with cool blue rune accent lighting, creating a consistent tone. The emotional tone remains consistently calm and focused.
shot1: Shot 1 begins with a fade-in, a wide eye-level composition showing the full stone tower workshop, foreground featuring a rough stone table, midground with soldering iron, rune circuit board, and clamping fixture, background revealing cold blue moonlight through arched windows and slowly flickering magical runes on the wall. Deep depth of field keeps both environment and tools sharp. Warm firelight illuminates the table edges while cool blue light outlines tool contours. An elderly male stands beside the table, firmly securing the work area and disconnecting power. The camera performs a slight push-in, helping viewers quickly grasp the safety starting point.
shot2: Shot 2 follows with a hard cut from the previous shot, transitioning to a close-up eye-level view focusing on the stone table surface. Solder wire spool, flux bottle, and tweezers are arranged diagonally, with the rune circuit board blurred in the background as a guide. Firelight remains the key light, with blue rune reflections on metallic edges. The instructor's fingers point to each tool in turn; objects emit subtle pixel shimmer when touched. Chinese voiceover simultaneously names their functions, maintaining a composed tone. The camera performs a short lateral slide, following the hand movement from left to right to complete the inventory.
shot3: Shot 3 transitions via hard cut to an extreme close-up from a slightly angled overhead perspective. Focus centers on the iron tip and damp cleaning sponge. Foreground shows the glowing iron tip, background softly blurred to retain flux bottle and stone texture. Warm light creates stable highlights on metal surfaces. The instructor first cleans the iron tip, then gently touches solder to the tip to form an even thin layer. Chinese The camera makes a slight tilt-down motion, pressing details more fully into frame.
shot4: Shot 4 continues with a hard cut to a medium-close overhead view using a tutorial-style top-down composition. Stone table edge forms a stable frame, hands centered in the image, wire, wire stripper, and circuit board pads clearly arranged front-to-back. Key light still comes from upper-right warm fire bowl, fill light from left-side blue rune lamp. The instructor first strips the wire to expose neat metal strands, then quickly pre-tins the pad with the iron. Both wire end and pad surface show uniform shiny thin solder layers. Chinese The camera remains stable, only making a minimal push-in to enhance step readability.
shot5: Shot 5 cuts via hard cut to a close-up eye-level view. Composition places the rune circuit board in the lower half of the frame, foreground slightly blurred with a short piece of solder wire, midground clearly showing hole positions, background revealing the instructor’s chest leather apron and flickering firelight. A resistor and an LED are picked up one by one, oriented correctly, and inserted into board holes. The moment component leads pass through holes aligns clearly with pixelated copper traces on the board. Chinese The camera performs a slow lateral follow, ensuring finger, component, and hole relationships remain clear.
shot6: Shot 6 cuts via hard cut to an extreme close-up at a slightly upward-angled eye-level view. Pad and component lead occupy the center of frame, shallow depth of field blurring the workshop background into soft pixel blocks. Iron tip enters from the right side, contacting both pad and lead simultaneously. Then solder is fed from the left. Upon heating, solder flows, spreads, and contracts into a full, conical joint. This material transformation is the focal point of this shot. The instructor emphasizes “烙铁同时碰焊盘和引脚”, with sentence timing perfectly aligned to the moment the iron touches. The camera performs a very short push-in, enhancing the credibility of the joint formation detail.
shot7: Shot 7 connects via hard cut to a medium eye-level shot beginning a dolly move. Composition smoothly shifts from one side of the board to the other. Foreground occasionally sweeps past tweezers and snips, adding speed layering. Midground continuously locks onto the soldering area. Warm firelight maintains table clarity, blue fill light outlines edges. The instructor completes the other side using the same method, then cleanly clips excess leads with snips. Metal fragments bounce to the edge of the stone table. Movements are fluid and controlled. Chinese voiceover briefly supplements the trimming step.
shot8: Shot 8 cuts via hard cut to an extreme close-up overhead view. Centered are several completed joints. Foreground shows magnifier frame edge, background displays faint rune patterns. Lighting remains consistent, with slightly enhanced highlight reflection on joint surfaces. The instructor gently prods components with tweezers to confirm stability, then checks each joint for fullness, roundness, absence of cold solder or bridging. Joint surfaces display clear light-dark block changes in pixel art style. Chinese Camera nearly static, only making a tiny zoom-in to enhance inspection feel.
shot9: Shot 9 connects via a gentle fade-in/fade-out transition, shifting to a close-up eye-level view with rapid push-in. The rune circuit board at the center of the stone table becomes the main subject again. Foreground shows power switch, background reveals the elderly male’s facial outline with satisfied smile. Warm firelight illuminates his wrinkles, cool blue rune light gradually lights up the board in grid pattern. After he turns on the power, runes glow steadily rather than flicker, component operation status clearly visible. In the final half-second, the camera freezes between the glowing circuit board and his smile, forming a complete, coherent, executable tutorial ending.
